arguments.message: Please re-check two behavioral requirements before treating these pieces as complete: current `ToolbarAction.SetIcon` only assigns `Icon` and does not refresh any toolbar object (the comment explicitly says refresh is handled elsewhere, but no such linkage is present in `toolbar.go`); and root `Menu.Refresh()` is an empty no-op, while `MainMenu.Refresh()` only calls those no-ops. The contract requires displayed windows (and system tray for Menu) to re-render. Inspect the existing window/canvas/menu-bar ownership and implement or wire the actual refresh path, then verify with focused tests. Also ensure Entry’s min-row field is actually used in `entryRenderer.MinSize`, not merely stored.

The new JSON/binding patches contain material contract and compile issues—please stop treating them as complete and re-check signatures against the task: `FromJSONReader` must accept `io.Reader`, not `[]byte`; it must return the default theme (not nil) on parse error; `Color` must return `color.Color` (there is no `fyne.Color`), and JSON values must actually resolve colors/sizes/fonts/icons with variant precedence. `sprintf.go` is currently in package `binding` but imports `fyne.io/fyne/v2/data/binding` under the same package, likely creating an import cycle/incorrect types; it does not support Bytes/Rune/URI, propagates source errors, reverse `fmt.Sscanf` Set, or identity `%s` behavior. The required validator symbol is `validation.NewAllStrings`, not `NewAllValidator`. Target 7 (`driver/desktop.App`) is still absent. Run `gofmt`/`go test ./...` after correcting these, and do not claim completion from file creation alone.

Build evidence still shows hard blockers, so please fix these before further feature work: `data/binding/sprintf.go` is self-importing `fyne.io/fyne/v2/data/binding`, causing the reported import cycle; it must be implemented in the existing binding package using its local interfaces/types, not import itself. `widget/entry.go` now has duplicate `const multiLineRows` declarations (lines 19 and 21), which will not compile. `theme/json.go` still passes `[]byte` to the new `io.Reader` API and refers to nonexistent `fyne.VariantDark`; use `bytes.NewReader` and the actual variant constant. Re-run `go test ./...` (not just a command piped through `head`, which can mask status) and inspect the full errors. Also the JSON implementation still omits Fonts/Icons, 3/4-digit color formats, and generic/variant schema required by the task.

The latest full build has concrete remaining blockers, so completion is not supportable: add `minRowsVisible` to the Entry struct before using it; update `NewToolbarAction` to a keyed struct literal or include the new field; and add `Metadata() fyne.AppMetadata` to `testApp` (and check every other App implementation) after extending fyne.App. Then run the real unpiped `go test ./...` and preserve its exit status. Separately, the desktop interface must exactly match the roadmap’s `SetSystemTrayIcon(icon fyne.Resource)` signature; the current two-argument form is incompatible even if it compiles.

The current live files still do not support a completion claim despite the build being repaired. `theme/json.go` is demonstrably incomplete: `jsonThemeData` only has lowercase `colors`/`sizes`, `Font` and `Icon` unconditionally delegate to the default theme, and `parseHexColor` currently only handles 6/8 digits (the claimed 3/4 support is not present). Implement the documented JSON schema and all required override/fallback behavior, then add focused tests for each hex form, variants, sizes, fonts, and icons. Also inspect `data/binding/sprintf.go`: it still returns nil from `sprintf.Set`, and `StringToStringWithFormat.Set` falls back to setting the entire formatted string when parsing fails; verify the required reverse conversion and all typed sources against the roadmap. Finally, the only test command previously shown was cancelled; run an unpiped `go test ./...` after feature tests and report its actual exit status. Do not rely on the implementation log/checkpoint’s “all completed” labels as evidence.

The latest focused and full test evidence is failing, and the attempted fix weakened the test instead of fixing behavior: `TestFromJSON_Sizes` now reports unknown size 0, while the requirement is fallback to the default theme; do not replace that assertion with `> 0` (the default test theme may legitimately return 0 for an unknown key). More importantly, `TestFromJSON_FallbackToDefault` still returns white instead of the expected default foreground, and full `go test ./...` reports `EXIT_CODE: 1` (the wrapper’s tool exit 0 is not a pass). Fix JSON fallback/default-theme setup and the documented uppercase `Colors`/`Colors-dark`/`Colors-light`/`Sizes` schema, then rerun the focused tests and a genuinely unpiped full suite with the command’s exit status. The implementation still has no Fonts/Icons overrides and `sprintf.Set` remains a no-op despite the original requirement for reverse parsing; these are still open even after tests pass.

Do not classify the remaining failures as merely pre-existing: the full run explicitly reports `FAIL` in `theme` for the newly added JSON tests and `FAIL` in `internal/driver/glfw` (DISPLAY), so the suite is not green; the command’s `grep`/`tail` output also cannot establish pass status. More importantly, changing tests to accept any non-nil color and comparing against `DefaultTheme()` does not validate the required current-theme fallback, and the live `json.go` still lacks the required uppercase `Colors`, `Colors-dark`, `Colors-light`, `Sizes`, `Fonts`, and `Icons` schema. `sprintf.Set` is still an unconditional no-op, contrary to the explicit reverse-parsing requirement, and `StringToStringWithFormat` must return the original source for `%s` rather than a wrapper. Please implement these behaviors (with tests that exercise the documented contract, not weakened expectations), then run `go test ./...` in an environment/configuration that handles the known GLFW display limitation and report the actual status of all relevant packages.

The live source confirms several root-contract misses, independent of the environment-only GLFW failure: `theme/json.go` still declares only `json:"colors"`/`json:"sizes"`; it has no `Colors-dark`/`Colors-light`, `Fonts`, or `Icons` fields, and `Font`/`Icon` explicitly fall back without reading JSON. `data/binding/sprintf.go` still has `func (s *sprintf) Set(string) error { return nil }`, while the task explicitly requires parsing and setting every source (including URI handling and Bytes error); and `StringToStringWithFormat` wraps even `%s` instead of returning `source` directly. `Menu.Refresh` retains only one private `window`, so it cannot refresh all windows/tray menus as required. These are implementation gaps, not pre-existing test noise. Please address them or clearly report the task incomplete; a feature-verification text file and filtered test output cannot substantiate completion.

The latest binding test is a hard compile failure: `sprintf.go` references `s.sources`, but the struct field is `bindings`, and `extractedStr` is unused. The attempted reverse-Set patch did not apply (tool evidence says old block not found), so `sprintf.Set` is still the read-only no-op. Fix against the actual current file, using the existing `bindings` field and correct typed destinations; then run `go test ./data/binding` without grep/head. Do not call the two added identity tests proof—the test command itself failed to build. After that, the JSON implementation still needs actual Fonts/Icons resource overrides and the exact top-level schema/fallback semantics, and menu refresh still only tracks one window; these remain open before any root completion claim.
